The game itself is great. I'm posting a negative review just to vent about the long, unskippable free-roam questlines. Holy sh!t, I've never seen such mediocre, nonsensical drivel in my life.
Start with this: the moment you talk to any NPC, they launch into their entire life story, and you can't skip it. That would be fine if there were even a breadcrumb of something engaging, funny, or thought-provoking in there. There isn't. Nothing. Every time an NPC opens their mouth, I suddenly want to go wash dishes or take out the trash, because both are more entertaining than this low-effort yapping.
Then there are the questlines themselves. For example, the very first one is a love triangle between three old geezers, delivered in the flattest, most uninspired way imaginable:
1. Grandpa A asks you to find missing Grandpa B, who's married to Grandma C.
2. Grandma C thinks Grandpa A killed Grandpa B and hates him for it.
3. While searching for Grandpa B, you find a locket containing the item Grandpa A once used to propose to Grandpa B's wife (Grandma C).
4. Grandma C is now in love with Grandpa A. Everyone's happy.
Huh?
On top of that, all of it is buried under nonstop filler dialogue. This isn't the millennial style where a character cracks a "witty" line every other sentence -- here it's more like every tenth line, and the rest is just empty, useless filler you're forced to sit through unless you mute it in the settings (thank god that's an option). Imagine being tied to a chair while the most untalented, forgettable writer alive reads you his debut novel -- that's the experience. It would almost be better if the dialogue were so bad it was funny, at least that'd be entertaining. Instead it's just bad -- painfully, soul-crushingly mediocre.
None of this would matter if it were skippable, but it isn't. You'll sit for five minutes listening to a rightfully bored voice actor read boring lines, over and over. And then there's the back-and-forth between loading zones, because NPCs always need to tell you something in person -- even though they had no problem calling you thirty seconds earlier.
Why do so many good games have this one spoonful of pure idiocy sitting right in the middle of otherwise solid design?

My first experience with this type of game was Baldur's Gate 3, which I absolutely loved. I had never played anything like it before, so I had completely ignored Divinity: Original Sin 2 when it came out. The announcement of Larian's next Divinity game was also a big factor in finally deciding to give DOS2 a try.
And it did not disappoint. I really enjoyed it.
It is noticeably inferior to Baldur's Gate 3 in terms of quality of life, which can sometimes make DOS2 feel a little frustrating after coming from BG3. But that's understandable given that it's an older game and simply shows the natural evolution of the genre and Larian's games.
Aside from that, the games are very similar, while DOS2 also has some of its own systems that are different rather than better or worse.
I'm very glad I played it, and now I'm even more excited for Larian's next Divinity game.
If you've played Baldur's Gate 3 but skipped Divinity: Original Sin 2 because you think it's too old, don't. It's a great game, and if you enjoyed BG3, you'll easily get another 100 hours of enjoyment out of it.

I must say, after spending a week jumping through timelines, this game has hit the absolute sweet spot of the genre. From my perspective, it’s exactly what I’ve been looking for - it’s deeper than Diablo but you don’t need a PhD to understand the builds like in Path of Exile. Visually, everything is just so cozy and the animations are satisfyingly crunchy, which really hooked me from the start. The coolest part of the whole experience is easily the time-travel narrative. How they executed the world changing between eras like the Divine and Ruined Future is just insanely cool; you visit the same locations, but everything is cooked in the future, making it feel like a fresh discovery every time.
I played as a Necromancer, and I was really glad to see, that minion build is working, I think minions gameplay will be my playstyle forever now xD. The skill system is super cool because it’s basically a build inside the build - every skill has its own tree, and you have some TitanQuestlike passive trees which are not overwhelming you.
The core of grind games is incredible (forging and looting). The forge is simple but deep, and features like the built-in loot filter are things every game in this genre deserves. Also closer to the end I found even more ways to create weapons like set items shards which can make set item from anything, recraft of potential, improve of no potent items, and a many more things which do everything possible for you to craft your perfect build. If you have enough time of course :)
I’m giving this one a 10/10. Let’s be honest, if I sometimes get bored of the grind because I’m a story-focused player, that’s on me, not the game. For what it tries to be, I found nothing bad here. It’s an amazing experience, and I’m definitely keeping it as my filler game between big projects.
